practice_blueprints.title: Law & Business scenario practice
practice_blueprints.summary: Generate original contractor business-law scenarios across the seven CSLB study-guide sections.

practice_blueprints.title: GE NEC navigation sprints
practice_blueprints.summary: Generate original open-book navigation drills that score topic classification, lookup-route choice, exception awareness, and final verification separately.

practice_blueprints.title: Electrical calculation ladder
practice_blueprints.summary: Generate stepwise original calculation drills from unit conversion to Ohm's Law, power, conductor/raceway reasoning, motors, transformers, and estimating arithmetic.

practice_blueprints.title: Testing and troubleshooting scenarios
practice_blueprints.summary: Generate original troubleshooting scenarios that require safety check, symptom classification, measurement choice, likely-cause reasoning, and verification.

practice_blueprints.title: Public works compliance scenarios
practice_blueprints.summary: Generate original Law & Business scenarios for public works contractor registration, prevailing wage, apprenticeship duties, and certified payroll recognition.

practice_blueprints.title: Error clinic and remediation loop
practice_blueprints.summary: Generate a short review session from the learner's last two error tags, then give one targeted reteach and two new original checks.
generation_rules: Never simply repeat the missed item.
Name the exact error tag before reteaching.
Keep the remediation task small enough to finish in one turn.
Advance only after the learner passes a similar-but-new check.

practice_blueprints.title: Worked-example ladder
practice_blueprints.summary: Generate a three-step worked example: model the first step, ask the learner for the next step, then ask a parallel multiple-choice item.
generation_rules: Use concrete numbers or facts only when they are original and source-safe.
Make the first example easier than the final quick check.
Explain why each distractor is attractive but wrong.
Use units and plain-language interpretation.

practice_blueprints.title: Feynman explain-back with optional quiz
practice_blueprints.summary: Ask the learner to explain a concept in plain language, but allow a multiple-choice fallback when free response would slow momentum.
generation_rules: Use free response for concept consolidation, not as a mandatory gate after every mini-lesson.
Offer multiple-choice or true/false when the learner needs faster progress.
Require explain-back only for repeated misconceptions or readiness checkpoints.
Keep feedback direct and specific.

practice_blueprints.title: Mock debrief and next-plan generator
practice_blueprints.summary: After a sectional or mixed mock, generate a concise score review, top error tags, and the next three study actions.
generation_rules: Do not report only a raw score.
Separate knowledge, calculation, reading, navigation, safety, and pacing errors.
Recommend the smallest useful next session.
Keep official exam logistics source-backed.

practice_blueprints.title: Spaced mixed review
practice_blueprints.summary: Generate a short mixed review that includes one old mastered item, one recent lesson item, and one weak-tag remediation item.
generation_rules: Include at least one item from a previous module when possible.
Make review short enough to appear after a normal lesson.
Prefer multiple-choice or true/false for fast checks.
Use free response only when a concept needs explanation.

practice_blueprints.title: Entrance Exam rotating section drill
practice_blueprints.summary: Rotate one focused section per day across math, numerical reasoning, reading, mechanical, and spatial skills.
generation_rules: Use only original practice items, never recalled or copyrighted exam questions.
Start each drill with the method card for that section.
Require explanation only after repeated misses or at checkpoint moments.
Attach an error label to every wrong answer.

practice_blueprints.title: Entrance math without answer choices
practice_blueprints.summary: Generate numeric-fill arithmetic and algebra items so the learner cannot rely only on elimination.
generation_rules: Ask for the numeric answer first, then optionally show choices.
Keep arithmetic realistic for aptitude speed practice.
Include one ratio, one percent, one algebra setup, and one rate item per set.

practice_blueprints.title: Entrance reading evidence set
practice_blueprints.summary: Generate short technical passages that require locating evidence, handling qualifiers, and rejecting unsupported choices.
generation_rules: Use short original passages about workplace instructions, scheduling, safety notices, or tool handling.
Do not require outside electrical knowledge.
After grading, identify the controlling phrase in the passage.

practice_blueprints.title: Mechanical and spatial reasoning lab
practice_blueprints.summary: Generate visual-thinking drills for levers, gears, pulleys, rotation, reflection, and paper folding.
generation_rules: Keep diagrams textual or simple ASCII when no image renderer is available.
Grade the reasoning step, not only the final letter.
Separate mechanical misses from spatial misses in the error log.

learning_activity_templates.title: Mini-lesson followed by one quick check
learning_activity_templates.summary: Default beginner flow for a new concept or procedure.
steps: State the practical job or exam situation in one paragraph.
Teach the smallest useful concept with one original example.
Register one four-option quick check with one best answer.
If correct, move to the next learning objective; if incorrect, explain the error pattern and ask one replacement check.
learner_action: Continue to the next objective after feedback.
feedback_rule: Do not ask the learner to choose the assessment format.
Do not chain multiple quizzes after a correct early answer.
Use free response only for review checkpoints, fragile understanding, or learner request.
exam_alignment: Matches multiple-choice exam rhythm while keeping Tutor teaching first.

learning_activity_templates.title: Worked example with hidden next step
learning_activity_templates.summary: Use for calculations, ratios, Ohm's Law, power, estimating, and blueprint arithmetic.
steps: Show the original scenario and identify known quantities.
Work the first step aloud.
Ask the learner to choose the next operation or expression.
Reveal the calculation and connect the result back to units and plausibility.
learner_action: Estimate whether the answer is reasonable.
feedback_rule: When the learner misses, identify whether the error was concept, setup, unit conversion, arithmetic, or answer-choice trap.
exam_alignment: Supports aptitude math, C-10 estimating math, and electrical calculation fluency.

learning_activity_templates.title: Open-book NEC navigation rehearsal
learning_activity_templates.summary: Use for GE objectives where the learner must look up code efficiently rather than rely only on memory.
steps: Present an original code-style scenario without copyrighted code text.
Ask the learner to classify the topic and predict the likely lookup area.
Ask what type of reference element matters: definition, article rule, table, note, or exception.
Close with a quick check about the navigation decision, not a copied code answer.
learner_action: Explain what evidence would confirm the answer.
feedback_rule: Track concept accuracy and lookup strategy separately.
Never reproduce NEC full text as course content.
exam_alignment: Matches GE open-book preparation where test materials are provided at the test site.

learning_activity_templates.title: Contractor scenario judgment
learning_activity_templates.summary: Use for C-10 trade judgment, Law & Business, safety, public works, contracts, liens, and employee topics.
steps: Present a realistic original contractor scenario.
Ask who has the obligation and what decision must be made.
Offer four answer choices with plausible distractors.
Explain why the best answer fits the role, timing, document, or safety obligation.
feedback_rule: Contrast the selected wrong answer with the best answer using one concrete distinction.
exam_alignment: Matches closed-book CSLB trade and Law & Business multiple-choice style without using leaked or recalled questions.

learning_activity_templates.title: Flashcard ladder for vocabulary and distinctions
learning_activity_templates.summary: Use when a learner needs fast recognition of terms before scenario practice.
steps: Show one term or pair of confusing terms.
Ask the learner to choose the best short meaning or distinction.
Promote correct cards into spaced review and keep missed cards in the current set.
After three correct cards, return to lesson or scenario practice.
feedback_rule: Keep flashcard sessions short; do not replace applied practice with memorization.
exam_alignment: Useful for vocabulary-heavy topics such as safety terms, plan symbols, business roles, and code navigation terms.

learning_activity_templates.title: Timed mixed set
learning_activity_templates.summary: Use after basic accuracy is stable, especially for aptitude, GE sectional practice, C-10, and Law & Business review.
steps: Select a small mixed set aligned to the current track.
Use a time budget that is short enough to reveal pacing habits.
Grade for accuracy and error type.
Send the learner back to the weakest lesson card or drill.
feedback_rule: Do timed sets only after the learner has seen the relevant mini-lessons.
Do not treat speed as mastery when conceptual accuracy is unstable.
exam_alignment: Supports timed aptitude preparation and later mock-exam readiness.

learning_activity_templates.title: Field visualization prompt
learning_activity_templates.summary: Use for circuits, raceways, boxes, panels, grounding, tools, jobsite safety, and troubleshooting.
steps: Describe a simple field situation with physical components.
Ask the learner to visualize current path, conductor route, equipment position, or hazard.
Change one condition and ask what changes.
Close with one safety or plausibility check.
learner_action: Predict the effect of changing one condition.
Connect the visual model to a rule or calculation.
feedback_rule: If the learner is confused, return to a simpler physical model before formulas.
exam_alignment: Supports mechanical reasoning, circuits, rough wiring, troubleshooting, and safety scenario questions.

learning_activity_templates.title: Document evidence coach
learning_activity_templates.summary: Use for PEF, GE experience, contractor qualifying experience, and learner readiness evidence.
steps: Ask the learner what claim they need to support.
List acceptable evidence categories at a high level without giving legal advice.
Separate documented, partially documented, and unsupported claims.
Create the next study or documentation task.
feedback_rule: Keep eligibility and documentation guidance separate from exam teaching.
Tell the learner to verify formal requirements with the official administering body.
exam_alignment: Supports application readiness for apprenticeship, GE, and contractor paths.

scenario_cards.title: Aptitude ratio: wire bundles
scenario_cards.summary: Original aptitude-style ratio scenario for beginner arithmetic practice.
scenario: A trainee sorts wire bundles. For every 3 small bundles, there are 2 large bundles. If there are 30 bundles total, how many are large?
correct_rationale: The ratio has 5 total parts. 30 divided by 5 is 6 per part. Large bundles are 2 parts, so 12.
distractor_rationales: 10 treats large bundles as one third of the total.
15 assumes half the bundles are large.
18 uses the small-bundle part instead of the large-bundle part.

scenario_cards.title: Aptitude math: percentage increase
scenario_cards.summary: Original percentage problem for fast arithmetic setup.
scenario: A practice score rises from 40 correct answers to 50 correct answers. What is the percent increase?
correct_rationale: The increase is 10 over the old value 40, so 10/40 = 25%.
distractor_rationales: 10% uses the raw increase as a percent.
20% divides by the new value incorrectly.
50% treats the new score as the increase.

scenario_cards.title: Aptitude algebra: missing cable length
scenario_cards.summary: Original algebra setup problem for word-problem translation.
scenario: A trainee cuts a cable into two pieces. The longer piece is 3 feet more than twice the shorter piece. Together they are 24 feet. How long is the shorter piece?
correct_rationale: Let x be the shorter piece. x + (2x + 3) = 24, so 3x = 21 and x = 7.
distractor_rationales: 9 ignores the extra 3 feet.
10.5 halves the remaining length too early.
15 is the longer piece when the shorter is 6, not a valid setup.

scenario_cards.title: Numerical reasoning: alternating sequence
scenario_cards.summary: Original sequence problem for recognizing two interleaved rules.
scenario: Find the next number: 2, 10, 4, 20, 6, 30, __
correct_rationale: Odd positions go 2, 4, 6, 8 while even positions go 10, 20, 30.
distractor_rationales: 32 continues neither interleaved rule.
40 would be the next even-position value after 30, not the next term here.
60 doubles 30 but ignores the alternating pattern.

scenario_cards.title: Numerical reasoning: table rate
scenario_cards.summary: Original table-reading problem focused on choosing the correct denominator.
scenario: A crew installs 48 fixtures in 6 hours on Monday and 54 fixtures in 9 hours on Tuesday. Which day had the higher fixtures-per-hour rate?
choices: D) Cannot compare because totals differ
correct_rationale: Monday is 48/6 = 8 fixtures per hour. Tuesday is 54/9 = 6 fixtures per hour. Monday is higher.
distractor_rationales: Tuesday has more total fixtures but a lower hourly rate.
Same rate ignores hours.
Rates can compare different totals when units match.

scenario_cards.title: Reading comprehension: sequence words
scenario_cards.summary: Original technical-reading item focused on before/after qualifiers.
scenario: Passage: Before a tool is returned to storage, it must be wiped clean and inspected for visible damage. If damage is found, report it to the supervisor instead of placing the tool back on the shelf. According to the passage, what happens before storage?
choices: A) Wipe and inspect the tool
B) Report every tool whether damaged or not
C) Place damaged tools directly on the shelf
D) Skip inspection if the tool looks clean
correct_rationale: The passage says the tool must be wiped clean and inspected before return to storage.
distractor_rationales: Only damaged tools are reported.
Damaged tools are not placed back on the shelf.
The passage requires inspection.

scenario_cards.title: Mechanical reasoning: lever effort
scenario_cards.summary: Original mechanical reasoning scenario for pivot-distance intuition.
scenario: Two workers use the same pry bar. Worker A pushes close to the pivot. Worker B pushes farther from the pivot with the same force. Who creates more turning effect?
choices: C) Both always create zero turning effect
D) Distance from pivot never matters
correct_rationale: With the same force, pushing farther from the pivot creates more turning effect.
distractor_rationales: Closer to the pivot gives less turning effect for the same force.
The pry bar can create turning effect.
Distance from pivot is central to lever reasoning.

scenario_cards.title: Mechanical reasoning: gear direction
scenario_cards.summary: Original gear-tracing item.
scenario: Gear A meshes directly with Gear B, and Gear B meshes directly with Gear C. If Gear A turns clockwise, which direction does Gear C turn?
correct_rationale: A makes B turn counterclockwise; B makes C turn clockwise.
distractor_rationales: Counterclockwise describes Gear B, not Gear C.
Meshed gears can transmit motion.
Direction is traceable from the gear connections.

scenario_cards.title: Mechanical reasoning: pulley tradeoff
scenario_cards.summary: Original pulley question about force-distance tradeoff.
scenario: A pulley setup reduces the force needed to lift a load. What tradeoff is usually introduced?
choices: A) More rope must be pulled
D) The rope no longer moves
correct_rationale: Pulley systems can reduce required force, but the user often pulls more rope distance.
distractor_rationales: Gravity does not disappear.
The load does not become weightless.
The rope must move for lifting to happen.

scenario_cards.title: Spatial reasoning: rotation versus mirror
scenario_cards.summary: Original spatial reasoning item focused on a common trap.
scenario: A shape is rotated 90 degrees clockwise. Which property must remain true?
choices: A) Distances between features stay the same
B) The shape becomes a mirror image
C) The number of corners changes
correct_rationale: Rotation preserves distances and relationships between features.
distractor_rationales: A mirror image is reflection, not rotation.
Rotation does not change the number of corners.
Rotation does not make a feature disappear.

scenario_cards.title: Paper folding: one hole through layers
scenario_cards.summary: Original folding/unfolding reasoning item.
scenario: A square sheet is folded once in half. A hole is punched through both layers near the folded edge. After unfolding, what should you expect?
choices: A) Two holes mirrored across the fold line
D) Holes only outside the paper
correct_rationale: A punch through two folded layers appears as two mirrored holes after unfolding.
distractor_rationales: One hole ignores the second layer.
Unfolding does not erase punched holes.
The holes remain on the paper.

scenario_cards.title: Application readiness: document gate
scenario_cards.summary: Original admissions-readiness item about documents versus test prep.
scenario: A learner studies hard for the aptitude test but has not found algebra proof or a valid photo ID. What is the biggest risk?
choices: A) The application may not qualify for testing or later verification
B) Algebra proof is never relevant
C) A high score automatically replaces all documents
D) Photo ID matters only after becoming a contractor
correct_rationale: Required documents are part of admissions readiness; test prep and document proof must both be handled.
distractor_rationales: Algebra proof is a stated requirement in local apprenticeship instructions.
A test score does not replace required documentation.
Photo ID is part of application/test-day readiness, not only later contractor licensing.

scenario_cards.title: PEF evidence: supported claims
scenario_cards.summary: Original PEF scenario about accuracy and supporting documentation.
scenario: A learner has two months of warehouse work and one semester of construction class. What is the best PEF strategy?
choices: A) List only experiences that can be described accurately and support them with documents where available
B) Claim several years of electrical work to sound stronger
C) Leave all experience blank because it is not perfect
D) Submit unrelated files and hope they count
correct_rationale: The safest PEF strategy is accurate, documented evidence; Tutor should never encourage exaggeration.
distractor_rationales: Overstating experience can create accuracy problems.
Relevant experience should not be omitted just because it is beginner-level.
Unrelated files do not support the claimed experience.

scenario_cards.title: No-calculator math: percent discount
scenario_cards.summary: Original mental-math item for quick percent handling.
scenario: A $80 tool is marked 25% off. What is the sale price?
correct_rationale: 25% of $80 is $20, so the sale price is $80 - $20 = $60.
distractor_rationales: $20 is the discount, not the sale price.
$55 subtracts the wrong discount.
$100 increases the price instead of discounting it.

scenario_cards.title: Problem solving: shared work rate
scenario_cards.summary: Original quantitative-reasoning item about rate and time.
scenario: One trainee labels 12 boxes in 6 minutes. At the same rate, how many boxes can three trainees label in 10 minutes?
correct_rationale: One trainee labels 2 boxes per minute. Three trainees label 6 per minute. In 10 minutes, they label 60.
distractor_rationales: 20 is one trainee's 10-minute output.
36 mixes 12 boxes with 3 trainees.
120 doubles the correct group rate.

scenario_cards.title: Reading comprehension: EXCEPT qualifier
scenario_cards.summary: Original passage-evidence question with a qualifier trap.
scenario: Passage: Before using a ladder, inspect the feet, rungs, and locking spreaders. Do not use the ladder if any part is damaged. Which action is NOT supported by the passage?
choices: C) Use a ladder with damaged locking spreaders if the job is short
correct_rationale: The passage says not to use the ladder if any part is damaged, so option C is not supported.
distractor_rationales: Inspecting feet is directly supported.
Inspecting rungs is directly supported.
Rejecting a damaged ladder follows from the passage.

scenario_cards.title: Paper folding: two folds
scenario_cards.summary: Original spatial item for reverse unfolding.
scenario: A square is folded in half vertically, then in half horizontally. One hole is punched through all layers near the folded corner. How many holes appear after unfolding?
correct_rationale: Two folds create four layers, so one punch through all layers produces four holes when unfolded.
distractor_rationales: One ignores the layers.
Two accounts for only one fold.
Eight doubles the number of layers without support.

scenario_cards.title: Mechanical reasoning: four gear chain
scenario_cards.summary: Original gear-direction drill.
scenario: Four gears mesh in a straight chain: A with B, B with C, and C with D. If A turns clockwise, how does D turn?
choices: C) It reverses twice and stops
correct_rationale: Each mesh reverses direction: A clockwise, B counterclockwise, C clockwise, D counterclockwise.
distractor_rationales: Clockwise would fit C, not D.
The gears do not stop just because direction reverses.
Direction is traceable connection by connection.

scenario_cards.title: Mechanical reasoning: incline tradeoff
scenario_cards.summary: Original mechanical-intuition item.
scenario: A ramp lets a worker push a heavy box with less force than lifting it straight up. What tradeoff is most likely?
choices: A) The box travels a longer distance
B) The box loses all weight
C) The worker uses no energy
correct_rationale: An incline can reduce required force by spreading the lift over a longer distance.
distractor_rationales: The box does not become weightless.
Work still requires energy.
Gravity does not change direction.

scenario_cards.title: Numerical reasoning: table trend
scenario_cards.summary: Original table pattern item.
scenario: A table shows x values 1, 2, 3, 4 and y values 4, 7, 10, 13. Which rule fits?
correct_rationale: Each y value equals 3x + 1: 4, 7, 10, 13.
distractor_rationales: x + 3 only fits when x = 1.
2x + 2 fits the first value but not the trend.
4x fits only the first value.

scenario_cards.title: Timed strategy: skip rule
scenario_cards.summary: Original pacing scenario for preserving score under time pressure.
scenario: A learner spends four minutes on one folding question and still has no method. What is the best next move in a timed set?
choices: A) Mark it, choose a controlled guess if required, and move to easier points
B) Spend the rest of the test on it
C) Stop reading all remaining questions
correct_rationale: A planned skip rule protects easier points and keeps pacing under control.
distractor_rationales: Spending unlimited time harms the whole section.
Stopping wastes available points.
Erasing previous work does not solve the pacing issue.

scenario_cards.title: Ohm's Law: current change
scenario_cards.summary: Conceptual circuit reasoning without a calculator.
scenario: A circuit keeps the same voltage, but resistance increases. What should happen to current?
choices: C) Current stays exactly the same
D) Current becomes unrelated to voltage
correct_rationale: From V = I x R, if V stays fixed and R increases, I must decrease.
distractor_rationales: Increasing current would require voltage to rise or resistance to fall.
Current would stay the same only if the voltage changed with resistance.
Current remains related to voltage and resistance.

scenario_cards.title: NEC navigation: classify before lookup
scenario_cards.summary: Open-book navigation drill that avoids reproducing code text.
scenario: A GE practice question asks about an installation condition in a damp location. What is the best first move?
choices: A) Guess from a memorized number
B) Classify the location and equipment topic before choosing a reference route
D) Pick the most technical-looking answer
correct_rationale: Open-book navigation starts by classifying the topic and condition so the learner can choose the right reference route.
distractor_rationales: Guessing loses the advantage of open-book source use.
Definitions and exceptions often matter in location-based questions.
Technical-looking wording is not evidence.

scenario_cards.title: C-10 scenario: extra work request
scenario_cards.summary: Contract/change-order judgment scenario.
scenario: During a project, a customer asks the contractor to add several outlets not included in the agreed scope. What is the safest business habit before doing the extra work?
choices: A) Complete the extra work and hope payment is agreed later
B) Document and authorize the scope and price change before proceeding
C) Remove the original scope from the records
D) Treat it as a safety inspection issue only
correct_rationale: A change order habit protects scope, price, schedule, and expectations before extra work begins.
distractor_rationales: Doing work first creates payment and expectation risk.
Deleting the original scope destroys the reference point.
Safety may still matter, but the question is about scope change control.

scenario_cards.title: Career orientation: route choice
scenario_cards.summary: Original beginner scenario for choosing the right career track.
scenario: A learner has no electrical experience and wants paid training while learning the trade. Which route best matches that immediate goal?
choices: C) Public works payroll reporting first
correct_rationale: Apprenticeship entrance best matches paid training while learning for a beginner.
distractor_rationales: C-10 is a contractor path requiring broader eligibility and business responsibility.
Payroll reporting is a contractor compliance topic, not the beginner entry route.
A full mock does not replace choosing the right path.

scenario_cards.title: Foundation math: unit check
scenario_cards.summary: Original unit-conversion and plausibility scenario.
scenario: A learner calculates 6 feet + 18 inches as 24 feet. What error happened?
correct_rationale: 18 inches is 1.5 feet, so adding it as 18 feet is a unit conversion error.
distractor_rationales: No reading qualifier controls this calculation.
There are no gears in the scenario.
This is not an application deadline issue.

scenario_cards.title: GE sizing: route first
scenario_cards.summary: Original GE scenario about classifying a sizing question before lookup.
scenario: A practice item asks for the correct raceway choice under a specific installation condition. What should the learner identify first?
choices: A) The wiring method/raceway category and condition
B) The contractor payroll tax rate
correct_rationale: Raceway questions start by classifying the wiring method/raceway category and installation condition.
distractor_rationales: Payroll tax is a Law & Business topic.
Paper folding belongs to aptitude spatial reasoning.
Answer length is not evidence.

scenario_cards.title: C-10 estimating: markup versus margin
scenario_cards.summary: Original estimating scenario for business math awareness.
scenario: A contractor adds 20% to a $1,000 estimated cost to set a price of $1,200. Which concept was directly applied?
choices: B) Margin as percent of price
correct_rationale: The contractor added a percentage to cost, which is markup on cost.
distractor_rationales: Margin compares profit to selling price, not simply the added percent on cost.
Voltage drop is an electrical calculation topic.
Lockout/tagout is safety procedure.

scenario_cards.title: Public works: certified payroll clue
scenario_cards.summary: Law and Business public works recognition scenario.
scenario: A contractor is working on a public project and the prompt mentions worker classifications, hours, and wage reporting. Which topic family is most likely being tested?
choices: A) Certified payroll / prevailing wage compliance
correct_rationale: Public project context plus worker classifications, hours, and wage reporting points to public works payroll and wage compliance.
distractor_rationales: Paper folding belongs to aptitude testing.
Transformer voltage is an electrical theory/calculation topic.
Trim color is not the compliance family signaled by the facts.

scenario_cards.title: Safety: lockout/tagout first
scenario_cards.summary: Hazardous-energy safety scenario for troubleshooting habits.
scenario: A machine has stopped unexpectedly and a worker is preparing to service it. What concern should be addressed before hands-on work begins?
choices: A) Prevent unexpected energization and verify hazardous energy control
B) Choose the fastest replacement part
D) Start with business finance calculations
correct_rationale: Safety-first troubleshooting requires hazardous energy control before servicing or repair activity.
distractor_rationales: Speed is not the first concern when hazardous energy may be present.
Labels and procedures are part of hazard control.
Business finance is unrelated to the immediate safety decision.

scenario_cards.title: Foundation: power from voltage and current
scenario_cards.summary: Original calculation item for P = V x I setup.
scenario: A small load uses 120 volts and 2 amps. What is the power?
correct_rationale: Power equals voltage times current, so 120 x 2 = 240 watts.
distractor_rationales: 60 divides instead of multiplying.
122 adds voltage and current.
240 ohms uses the wrong unit for power.

scenario_cards.title: Foundation: series current path
scenario_cards.summary: Original concept item for circuit path recognition.
scenario: A circuit has only one path for current. If one load opens, all loads stop operating. Which circuit type is described?
correct_rationale: A series circuit has one current path, so an open interrupts the entire path.
distractor_rationales: Parallel circuits have multiple paths.
Public works is a contractor compliance topic.
PEF is an apprenticeship application evidence form.

scenario_cards.title: GE blueprint: study weighting
scenario_cards.summary: Original scenario about using official exam weights.
scenario: A GE learner has 10 study hours this week and wants to allocate by official emphasis. Which domain should usually get the largest block?
choices: D) Random equal time for every favorite topic
correct_rationale: The GE blueprint gives Installation the largest weight, so it should usually get the largest practice block.
distractor_rationales: Safety matters, but it is not the largest weighted domain.
Maintenance and Repair is smaller than Installation.
Blueprint weighting should guide allocation.

scenario_cards.title: GE mastery: lookup time
scenario_cards.summary: Original open-book readiness item.
scenario: A learner answers GE concept questions correctly but spends too long finding references during practice. What should be trained next?
choices: A) NEC navigation route and lookup speed
B) Ignore the issue because open-book means unlimited time
correct_rationale: Open-book exams still require efficient navigation and time control.
distractor_rationales: Open-book does not remove time pressure.
Leaked questions are unsafe and unreliable.
Calculations may still appear and should not be abandoned.

scenario_cards.title: C-10: rough wiring sequence
scenario_cards.summary: Original scenario about construction sequence reasoning.
scenario: A wall will soon be closed. Which task is most likely a rough-wiring priority before closure?
choices: A) Install concealed raceway or cable paths required behind the wall
B) Final decorative cover plates only
correct_rationale: Rough wiring includes infrastructure that must be in place before surfaces close.
distractor_rationales: Decorative cover plates are finish-stage work.
Certified payroll is a Law & Business public works topic.
Paper folding is an aptitude topic.

scenario_cards.title: C-10: special energy source
scenario_cards.summary: Original special-systems safety item.
scenario: A site has utility power plus a battery energy storage system. What assumption should the learner avoid?
choices: A) That turning off utility power removes every energy source
B) That labels and isolation matter
C) That stored energy can affect safety planning
D) That startup checks may be needed
correct_rationale: Battery storage can remain an energy source, so utility disconnect alone may not remove every hazard.
distractor_rationales: Labels and isolation do matter.
Stored energy can affect safety planning.
Startup checks may be needed.

scenario_cards.title: Law & Business: insurance versus lien
scenario_cards.summary: Original topic-classification scenario.
scenario: A prompt asks how a contractor manages payment-security rights after unpaid work. Which topic family is most likely?
correct_rationale: Payment-security rights point to mechanics lien concepts rather than insurance.
distractor_rationales: Insurance manages risk, not payment-security rights in this cue.
Paper folding is an aptitude task.
Parallel circuits are electrical theory.

scenario_cards.title: Law & Business: worker-status cue
scenario_cards.summary: Original employment scenario for classification practice.
scenario: A scenario focuses on who controls the worker's schedule, tools, supervision, and payroll treatment. Which Law & Business area is likely involved?
correct_rationale: Schedule, tools, supervision, and payroll treatment are worker-status and employment clues.
distractor_rationales: Raceway fill is a trade/code topic.
Paper folding is aptitude spatial reasoning.
Gear ratio is mechanical reasoning.

scenario_cards.title: Math bridge: fraction to percent
scenario_cards.summary: Original numeric-fill item for fraction, decimal, and percent fluency.
scenario: A conduit run is 3/8 complete. What percent of the run is complete?
correct_rationale: 3 divided by 8 is 0.375, which is 37.5%.

scenario_cards.title: Math trap: percent base
scenario_cards.summary: Original multiple-choice item about percent increase base quantity.
scenario: A practice score rises from 24 correct to 30 correct. What is the percent increase?
correct_rationale: The increase is 6. The base is the original 24. 6/24 = 25%.

scenario_cards.title: Algebra setup: fittings count
scenario_cards.summary: Original equation-setup item for word-problem translation.
scenario: Box A has 12 more fittings than Box B. Together they have 64 fittings. Define x as the number in Box B and write the equation.
correct_rationale: Box B is x. Box A is x + 12. Together means add them to get 64.

scenario_cards.title: Rate reasoning: parts per hour
scenario_cards.summary: Original rate item for numerical computation.
scenario: A trainee labels 45 parts in 15 minutes. At the same rate, how many parts can the trainee label in 1 hour?
correct_rationale: One hour is four 15-minute blocks. 45 times 4 is 180.

scenario_cards.title: Numerical pattern: changing difference
scenario_cards.summary: Original sequence item using second differences.
scenario: Find the next number: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
correct_rationale: The differences are 3, 5, 7, 9, so the next difference is 11. 26 + 11 = 37.

scenario_cards.title: Reading qualifier: only after
scenario_cards.summary: Original passage-evidence item about sequence and condition words.
scenario: Passage: Submit the completed form only after the supervisor signs the verification line. Unsigned forms will be returned. Question: What must happen before submission?
choices: A) The applicant pays a fee
B) The supervisor signs the verification line
C) The form is copied twice
D) The applicant calls the office
correct_rationale: The controlling words are only after the supervisor signs the verification line.

scenario_cards.title: Reading EXCEPT: tool notice
scenario_cards.summary: Original EXCEPT item for careful answer-task handling.
scenario: Passage: Bring a photo ID, two pencils, and your appointment notice. Calculators and phones are not permitted in the testing room. Question: All are required EXCEPT:
correct_rationale: The question asks EXCEPT. A calculator is not permitted, not required.

scenario_cards.title: Mechanical: door hinge leverage
scenario_cards.summary: Original true-false item about pivot distance.
scenario: True or false: Pushing a door near the outer edge usually takes less force than pushing near the hinge.
correct_rationale: The outer edge is farther from the pivot, so the same push creates more turning effect.

scenario_cards.title: Mechanical: ramp tradeoff
scenario_cards.summary: Original mechanical reasoning item about force and distance tradeoff.
scenario: Two ramps reach the same platform. Ramp A is short and steep. Ramp B is longer and less steep. Which usually requires less pushing force for the same load?
choices: C) Both always require exactly the same force
D) Neither because ramps do not affect force
correct_rationale: The longer, less steep ramp usually reduces force but increases travel distance.

scenario_cards.title: Mechanical: five-gear chain
scenario_cards.summary: Original gear-direction item using reversal count.
scenario: Gear A meshes with B, B with C, C with D, and D with E. If A turns clockwise, which direction does E turn?
choices: D) Cannot tell from the connections
correct_rationale: There are four gear contacts. Four reversals returns to the same direction as A.

scenario_cards.title: Spatial: rotated L shape
scenario_cards.summary: Original short-answer item distinguishing rotation from reflection.
scenario: An L shape has its short foot pointing right. After a 90-degree clockwise rotation, does that foot point down, left, up, or right?
correct_rationale: A right-pointing feature rotated 90 degrees clockwise points down.

scenario_cards.title: Paper folding: vertical then horizontal
scenario_cards.summary: Original paper-folding item using reverse unfold order.
scenario: A square paper is folded left-to-right, then bottom-to-top. One hole is punched near the final folded packet corner away from both fold lines. When unfolded, how many matching holes appear?
correct_rationale: Two folds create four layers at that position, so the hole mirrors into four positions when unfolded.

scenario_cards.title: Timed strategy: triage decision
scenario_cards.summary: Original pacing item for skip/mark/return behavior.
scenario: During a timed mixed set, you spend 90 seconds on a spatial item and still cannot choose between two answers. What is the best next action?
choices: A) Spend as long as needed
B) Mark it, make the best provisional choice if required, and move on
C) Stop the test and review notes
D) Guess without reading the remaining questions
correct_rationale: Pacing protects the total score. Mark, move, and return if time remains.

scenario_cards.title: PEF: specific evidence beats vague claims
scenario_cards.summary: Original PEF item about evidence quality.
scenario: Which PEF note is strongest?
choices: C) I completed a 40-hour safety course and can attach the certificate
correct_rationale: Specific, verifiable evidence is stronger than vague self-description.

flashcard_decks.title: Career orientation cues
flashcard_decks.summary: Cards for choosing the right learning route before studying details.
cards: Apprenticeship entrance: selection readiness, aptitude reasoning, and admissions documents.
General Electrician: California worker certification with qualifying experience and open-book exam navigation.
C-10: contractor trade classification with closed-book trade judgment.
Law & Business: contractor business exam covering organization, finance, employment, contracts, public works, and safety.
Eligibility: formal requirement; not the same as study readiness.
Blueprint: official topic map for practice weighting.

flashcard_decks.title: Electrical foundations vocabulary
flashcard_decks.summary: Short recognition cards for early electrical concepts.
cards: Voltage: electrical pressure that helps drive current.
Current: flow of electric charge.
Resistance: opposition to current flow.
Power: rate of electrical work or energy use.
Series circuit: one current path.
Parallel circuit: multiple current paths.

flashcard_decks.title: Foundation math and safety habits
flashcard_decks.summary: Cards for setup discipline, unit awareness, and safety-first thinking.
cards: Unknown: name what the problem asks for before calculating.
Unit conversion: convert inches, feet, amps, volts, watts, and percent before comparing.
Plausibility: estimate whether the answer could make sense.
Symptom: what is observed before troubleshooting.
Expected value: what a measurement should show if the system is normal.
Verify: prove a condition; do not merely assume it.

flashcard_decks.title: GE navigation vocabulary
flashcard_decks.summary: Terms for open-book code navigation and topic classification.
cards: Definition: a source-backed meaning that can change how a rule applies.
Article: a code organization unit for a topic family.
Table: structured values used for lookup or calculation.
Exception: a condition that changes a general rule.
Lookup route: the planned path from question facts to reference evidence.
Verification: checking the answer against the exact prompt conditions.

flashcard_decks.title: GE mastery dimensions
flashcard_decks.summary: Cards for separating GE readiness signals.
cards: Concept accuracy: can explain why an answer is plausible.
Topic classification: routes the question to the right domain.
Lookup route: finds the right reference path efficiently.
Calculation setup: uses correct units and quantity.
Timed accuracy: preserves correctness under section pressure.
Lookup time: measures open-book speed separately from knowledge.

flashcard_decks.title: C-10 trade practice cues
flashcard_decks.summary: Cards for contractor trade practice and closed-book judgment.
cards: Planning and estimating: read scope, plans, specs, quantity, material, labor, and risk.
Rough wiring: infrastructure before final surfaces and trim.
Finish wiring: devices, trim, labeling, terminations, testing, and handoff.
Startup/troubleshooting: symptom, safety, measurement, hypothesis, correction, verification.
Special systems: PV, generator, battery, and storage can remain energy sources.
Closed-book: build decision patterns, not lookup dependence.

flashcard_decks.title: Law and Business scenario cues
flashcard_decks.summary: Recognition cards for contractor business-law topic families.
cards: Bid: proposed price and scope before contract award.
Change order: documented change to agreed scope, price, or schedule.
Prevailing wage: wage compliance concept for public works.
Certified payroll: public works record/reporting concept.
Lien: payment-security topic family.
Insurance: risk-transfer topic family.

flashcard_decks.title: Apprenticeship math triggers
flashcard_decks.summary: Fast recognition cards for arithmetic and algebra prompts.
cards: Total parts: add all ratio parts before scaling.
Percent increase: increase divided by old value.
Percent multiplier: 1 plus or minus the percent as a decimal.
Per: divide to create a rate.
Twice: multiply the unknown by 2.
Remaining: total minus used amount.
Substitution: test answer choices in the equation when stuck.
Plausibility: estimate before trusting arithmetic.

flashcard_decks.title: Apprenticeship mechanical triggers
flashcard_decks.summary: Fast recognition cards for mechanical reasoning.
cards: Lever pivot: find the fulcrum first.
Longer lever arm: more turning effect for the same force.
Meshed gears: adjacent gears rotate opposite directions.
Three meshed gears: first and third rotate the same direction.
Pulley tradeoff: less force usually means more rope distance.
Incline tradeoff: less force over a longer distance.
Fluid level: connected open liquid surfaces tend to level.
Trace one connection at a time.

flashcard_decks.title: Apprenticeship spatial and reading triggers
flashcard_decks.summary: Fast recognition cards for paper folding, rotation, and technical reading.
cards: Rotation: relationships stay the same; orientation changes.
Reflection: mirror image across a line.
Fold line: marks reflect across it when unfolded.
Layer count: one punch can create multiple holes.
Unfold order: reverse the folding order.
Passage evidence: answer from text, not outside knowledge.
Qualifier: words like except, only, always, before, after matter.
Unsupported choice: sounds reasonable but adds a claim not in the passage.

flashcard_decks.title: Apprenticeship document readiness
flashcard_decks.summary: Recognition cards for admissions paperwork and official-instruction habits.
cards: Photo ID: required identity evidence for application/test-day steps.
Algebra proof: transcript or approved equivalent showing required math background.
Original documents: may be required later for verification even after online upload.
Veteran waiver: only applies when documented criteria are met.
Official email: controls scheduling details and deadlines.
Portal checklist: track uploaded, submitted, confirmed, and pending items.

flashcard_decks.title: PEF evidence habits
flashcard_decks.summary: Cards for turning experience into accurate, supported PEF claims.
cards: Claim: one experience statement the learner can describe accurately.
Evidence: a document that supports a claim.
Unsupported claim: may receive no credit or create review problems.
Deadline window: complete and submit before the official cutoff.
Work history: hours, employer, role, and supporting proof.
Training history: courses, certificates, transcripts, and completion evidence.

flashcard_decks.title: Aptitude test-day strategy
flashcard_decks.summary: Cards for pacing, instructions, and final-week execution.
cards: Classify first: name the section before solving.
Easy points first: do not let one hard item consume the section.
Controlled guess: eliminate impossibilities before choosing under time pressure.
No-calculator mode: practice arithmetic cleanly unless official instructions allow tools.
Qualifier scan: mark words like except, only, before, and after.
Error tag: convert each miss into a repair action.

flashcard_decks.title: Entrance Exam format mix
flashcard_decks.summary: Cards reminding Tutor and learner to practice more than multiple choice.
cards: Multiple choice: fast grading and elimination practice.
Numeric fill: prevents overreliance on answer choices.
Short evidence answer: proves reading support.
True/false: quick concept check, but explain false statements after misses.
Visual reasoning prompt: trace one feature, fold, gear, or force path.
Never call original Tutor items official or recalled exam questions.

flashcard_decks.title: Entrance reading qualifier traps
flashcard_decks.summary: Recognition cards for passage-based reading questions.
cards: only
except
unless
before
after
must
may
not permitted
first
most likely

flashcard_decks.title: Entrance mechanical motion cues
flashcard_decks.summary: Fast cues for tracing basic mechanical systems.
cards: Pivot: farther usually means less force.
Ramp: less force usually means more distance.
Meshed gear: reverse direction.
Even gear reversals: same final direction.
Odd gear reversals: opposite final direction.
Pulley advantage: less force, more rope travel.

flashcard_decks.title: Entrance spatial and paper-folding cues
flashcard_decks.summary: Fast cues for rotation, reflection, and unfolding.
cards: Rotation preserves feature order.
Reflection reverses handedness.
Track one asymmetric feature.
Unfold in reverse order.
Mirror holes across each fold line.
Count layers before counting holes.

readiness_checkpoints.title: Full course map checkpoint
readiness_checkpoints.summary: Use after orientation to confirm the learner understands the five modules and the next best study route.
checkpoint_prompts: Can the learner distinguish apprenticeship entrance, General Electrician certification, C-10 trade, and Law & Business?
Can the learner name why shared foundations come before advanced exam practice?
Can the learner explain why official blueprints and source versions control exam facts?
Can the learner state the learning loop: diagnostic, lesson, quick quiz, error tag, remediation, readiness gate?
mastery_evidence: learner can continue into either apprenticeship sprint or foundation lessons
remediation: If route confusion remains, return to career graph and route-choice scenarios.
If source confusion remains, return to official source discipline.
If learning-loop confusion remains, return to diagnostic readiness loop.

readiness_checkpoints.title: 14-day newcomer sprint checkpoint
readiness_checkpoints.summary: Use at the end of the two-week newcomer sprint to route the learner into apprenticeship final-week practice, GE foundations, C-10, or Law & Business.
checkpoint_prompts: Can the learner solve basic unit, ratio, percent, and algebra setup checks without repeated setup errors?
Can the learner explain voltage, current, resistance, power, and one current-path difference?
Can the learner answer reading and mechanical/spatial quick checks with a named method?
Can the learner classify whether the next route should be apprenticeship, GE, C-10, or Law & Business?
Does the learner have an error log and document checklist that can drive the next session?
mastery_evidence: 80% or better on foundation math quick checks
one correct Ohm's Law or circuit concept explanation
route choice matches learner goal and eligibility situation
error log has at least two actionable repair items
remediation: If setup errors remain, repeat worked-example ladder for units and algebra.
If concept language is weak, repeat explain-back with multiple-choice fallback.
If aptitude timing is weak, move to daily selection set before full timed practice.
If route choice is unclear, repeat career orientation cues and source discipline.

readiness_checkpoints.title: Foundations readiness checkpoint
readiness_checkpoints.summary: Use before moving from shared foundations into a specific track.
checkpoint_prompts: Explain voltage, current, resistance, and power without formulas first.
Solve one ratio/percentage question and state the unit.
Choose the safest first step in a basic troubleshooting scenario.
mastery_evidence: concept explanation is not purely memorized
remediation: Return to cec-lesson-ohms-law for concept confusion.
Return to cec-lesson-shared-math for setup or unit errors.
Return to cec-lesson-cal-osha-lockout for unsafe sequencing.

readiness_checkpoints.title: Apprenticeship entry sprint readiness checkpoint
readiness_checkpoints.summary: Use weekly for a learner taking apprenticeship selection early next month.
checkpoint_prompts: Can the learner solve ratio, percent, algebra setup, and rate questions without hints?
Can the learner identify difference, multiplication, alternating, and grouped sequence patterns?
Can the learner answer a technical-reading item using only passage evidence?
Can the learner trace lever, gear, pulley, rotation, and folding questions without guessing?
Can the learner complete a short mixed set without losing pacing discipline?
Has the learner prepared a PEF documentation inventory and official-instruction checklist?
mastery_evidence: 80% or better on recent arithmetic/algebra quick checks
70% or better on recent numerical reasoning cards
no repeated safety or documentation-boundary errors
remediation: If math misses dominate, return to arithmetic speed and algebra setup lessons.
If mechanical misses dominate, use field visualization and one-connection tracing.
If spatial misses dominate, drill rotation versus reflection and one-fold paper unfolding.
If reading misses dominate, drill qualifier words and passage-only evidence.
If pacing misses dominate, switch to timed mixed sets with fewer questions.

readiness_checkpoints.title: Apprenticeship final-week checkpoint
readiness_checkpoints.summary: Use when the learner is within roughly one week of an apprenticeship entrance selection event.
checkpoint_prompts: Can the learner complete a three-item quick quiz after each mini-lesson and explain every miss by error tag?
Can the learner solve ratio, percent, algebra, sequence, and table questions in no-calculator practice mode?
Can the learner answer reading questions using passage evidence and qualifier checks?
Can the learner trace one lever, one gear chain, one pulley or incline, and one paper-folding problem?
Can the learner state the planned skip/mark/return rule before a timed set starts?
Has the learner verified official test-day instructions, photo ID, application status, and PEF/document requirements?
mastery_evidence: at least 80% on the most recent math/numerical quick set
at least 70% on reading/mechanical/spatial quick sets
all misses have an error tag and next drill
final-day study plan avoids heavy new content
remediation: If math accuracy is low, run two short ratio/percent/algebra sets before mixed practice.
If reading errors include unsupported claims, repeat qualifier and evidence-elimination drills.
If mechanical or spatial tracing is unstable, slow down and narrate one connection or unfold at a time.
If documents are incomplete, stop study expansion and resolve official checklist items first.

readiness_checkpoints.title: GE navigation readiness checkpoint
readiness_checkpoints.summary: Use before GE sectional or full mock practice.
checkpoint_prompts: Classify three original GE prompts by blueprint domain.
For one open-book prompt, name the likely reference route before answering.
Explain one case where an exception or definition could change the answer.
mastery_evidence: awareness of definitions, tables, and exceptions
remediation: Return to cec-lesson-ge-blueprint for weighting confusion.
Return to cec-lesson-nec-navigation for lookup route errors.
Return to cec-lesson-conductors-raceways or cec-lesson-ge-installation for category errors.

readiness_checkpoints.title: C-10 and Law readiness checkpoint
readiness_checkpoints.summary: Use before mixed contractor exam practice.
checkpoint_prompts: Classify a contractor scenario as trade, business finance, employment, contract, lien, public works, or safety.
Solve one estimating setup and identify whether it uses markup, margin, tax, or quantity takeoff.
Choose the best first action in a change-order or safety scenario.
remediation: Return to cec-lesson-c10-estimating for math setup errors.
Return to cec-lesson-law-contracts-change-orders for scope-control errors.
Return to cec-lesson-public-works for compliance-cue misses.

readiness_checkpoints.title: Entrance Exam section readiness checkpoint
readiness_checkpoints.summary: Use after several Entrance Exam lessons to decide whether the learner needs focused repair or mixed timed practice.
checkpoint_prompts: Can the learner solve no-choice numeric-fill math items before seeing choices?
Can the learner name the pattern type in sequence and table questions?
Can the learner identify the exact passage phrase that controls a reading answer?
Can the learner trace lever, ramp, gear, pulley, rotation, and fold items one step at a time?
Can the learner explain the reason for a wrong answer using an error label?
Can the learner switch from focused drills to timed mixed sets without freezing?
mastery_evidence: 80% on math computation and setup drills across two sessions
75% on numerical pattern/table drills across two sessions
75% on reading evidence drills with qualifier traps
documented error log with fewer repeated misses
one completed timed mixed set with a written skip rule
remediation: If numeric fill is weak, return to fraction/decimal/percent bridges and equation setup.
If reading is weak, use evidence-ladder drills before more mixed practice.
If mechanical is weak, use force-distance and one-connection tracing drills.
If spatial is weak, separate rotation/reflection before paper-folding drills.
If timing is weak, shorten sets and enforce mark/move/return behavior.

error_taxonomy.title: Topic classification error
error_taxonomy.summary: The learner knows facts but routes the question to the wrong domain, code area, or Law and Business section.
remediation: Ask the learner to underline the clue that determines the topic family.
Use a two-choice classification drill before asking for the final answer.

error_taxonomy.title: Unit or setup error
error_taxonomy.summary: The learner starts calculation before converting units or identifying the requested quantity.
remediation: Require known/unknown/unit notation before arithmetic.
Use worked-example next-step prompts.

error_taxonomy.title: Safety sequencing error
error_taxonomy.summary: The learner chooses speed, replacement, or production before hazard control and verification.
remediation: Return to safety-first scenario cards.
Ask what could hurt a person or property before technical diagnosis.

error_taxonomy.title: Documentation boundary error
error_taxonomy.summary: The learner confuses learning readiness with formal eligibility, application evidence, or project documentation.
remediation: Separate study plan, eligibility, and official application steps.
Use document evidence coach templates.

error_taxonomy.title: Memorization over navigation
error_taxonomy.summary: The learner tries to memorize open-book answers instead of building a reliable lookup route.
remediation: Use NEC navigation rehearsal.
Score route choice separately from final answer.

claim_summaries: Inside Wireman applicants take an aptitude test with mathematical reasoning, numerical reasoning, reading comprehension, mechanical reasoning, and paper folding.
The aptitude test time is 2 hours 20 minutes.
The Personal Experience Form can constitute up to 40% of the final score.
GAN describes its Aptitude Battery as assessing basic math, reading, and spatial skills for apprentice selection.
GAN says the battery was developed from job analysis of skills and abilities required for school and job performance.
GAN states that its apprentice selection tests are reliable, valid, and used across multiple apprenticeship programs.
GAN offers an Aptitude Test Study Guide intended to familiarize applicants with test sections and practice-question types.
Tutor may reference the study-guide availability and broad preparation purpose, but must not reproduce paid study-guide content.
GAN explains validation as the process for making selection procedures fair, defensible, and predictive of successful apprentice and employee performance.
Tutor should teach PEF, aptitude, and interview preparation as evidence-based selection readiness, not as a way to game the process.
Electrical Training Alliance describes IBEW/NECA apprenticeship aptitude tests as validated tools for selecting apprentices.
Its sample-test guidance supports algebra/function and reading-comprehension practice shapes with one correct answer per sample item.
Tutor should use this as a topic-shape source only and generate original practice items.
CCETI describes a GAN Aptitude Test Battery with reading, numerical computation, numerical reasoning, paper folding, problem solving, and mechanical comprehension.
CCETI states that electrical construction knowledge is not part of its GAN aptitude test.
CCETI is a California JATC comparator for study design and test-day constraints, not the controlling LAETT Local 11 rule source.
Inland Electrical describes an ETA-style aptitude test with timed math and reading sections, no calculator, no guessing penalty, and interview progression after a qualifying score.
Tutor should treat this as a comparator for pacing and no-calculator practice, not as LAETT or GAN local policy.
California DIR says persons performing electrician work for a C-10 licensed contractor must be certified under DLSE standards.
Electrician certification and exam applications are available online; electrician trainee online registration is not yet available as of the materialized source snapshot.
DIR announced new procedures for exams taken on or after 2026-06-01 administered by CPS HR Consulting.
California electrician certification exams are open-book according to the DIR FAQ.
Test materials are provided at the test site.
DIR directs learners to the Test Info page and referenced content outline for study scope.
General Electrician exam has 100 questions.
General Electrician exam time is 4 hours 30 minutes.
General Electrician content outline weights are Safety 6%, Electrical System Requirements 22%, Installation 66%, Maintenance and Repair 6%.
General Electrician certification application requires 8,000 hours of qualifying work for an electrical contractor installing, constructing, or maintaining NEC-covered electrical systems.
DIR lists electrician categories including General Electrician, Residential Electrician, Fire/Life/Safety Technician, Voice Data Video Technician, and Non-residential Lighting Technician.
The category page distinguishes candidates with required experience, some experience, registered apprenticeship, and no experience or related instruction.

The ECCC general curriculum includes safety, tools/materials/handling, electrical theory, code requirements, conductors, raceways, lighting, overcurrent devices, grounding systems, plans/specifications, transformers, and testing.
Electrical theory topics include series, parallel, combination circuits, capacitance, rectifiers, harmonics, semiconductor devices, and amplifier basics.
Code-requirements training includes using a code book, recognizing definitions, exceptions, markings, wet/damp/dry locations, and special occupancies.
C-10 Electrical Study Guide blueprint applies to exams scheduled on or after 2024-06-01.
C-10 trade weights are Planning and Estimating 28%, Rough Wiring 27%, Finish Wiring and Trim 11%, Startup/Troubleshooting/Maintenance 16%, Safety 18%.
The C-10 trade examination is closed-book, multiple-choice, and has four choices per question.
Some C-10 questions require mathematical computation and a calculator is provided.

The Law and Business examination is divided into Business Organization and Licensing 13%, Business Finances 15%, Employment Requirements 20%, Insurance and Liens 12%, Contract Requirements and Execution 21%, Public Works 5%, and Safety 14%.
The Law and Business exam is closed-book, multiple-choice, and has four choices per question.
Some Law and Business questions require mathematical computation and a calculator is provided.
Contractor license applicants generally prepare for both the Law & Business examination and the trade examination.
CSLB study guides list topic areas, show approximate weights, include sample questions, and recommend resource materials.
CSLB says applicants must have at least four years of experience in the classification to qualify for the contractor examination.
Credit is given only for experience at journey level or as foreman, supervising employee, contractor, or owner-builder.
Education, technical training, or vocational training may receive credit up to three years, but at least one year must be practical experience.
